spoken_text: Mate, are you ok? I heard the collapse! The treasure should be just ahead. Be careful!
delivery_notes: Kit is unseen beyond the small grated WALL access panel. Start urgently, worried and on the edge of panic: 'Mate, are you ok?' is a genuine check for life, with a quick breath and strain in the voice rather than a cheerful greeting or a full scream. 'I heard the collapse!' carries the fear that prompted the call. Ease slightly into practical reassurance on 'The treasure should be just ahead', while still shaken; finish 'Be careful!' with protective urgency. Keep the words intelligible through the grate. Any stronger relief must follow a genuinely audible nearby player movement/footstep cue, never an assumed reply or unseen visual confirmation.

spoken_text: There you are. Still in one piece?
Stay clear. Rope coming down.
Steady. Catch your breath. Did you find it?
delivery_notes: Kit; first checking player, then curious

spoken_text: Let me see. Raise it.
Then we're not chasing a story anymore.
A start, then. Let's see where it leads.
Come on. There's a fire and a dry seat waiting in the village.
I'd forgotten how big the sky was.
delivery_notes: Kit; low, taking in the woods

spoken_text: Hold it there. There are marks under the moss.
A road to the treasury, perhaps. Someone in the village might read it.
I'll wait here.
There. Chimney smoke.
Right. I’m sitting down before I make this worse.
delivery_notes: Annoyed at the injury, not the player.

spoken_text: I won’t get far along those roads like this. You’ll have to go without me.
Bring what you find back here. I can still make myself useful.
delivery_notes: Already clearing a space on the table.

spoken_text: The tomb was there. So was something worth the climb.
delivery_notes: Modest pride; gestures towards the player’s find.

spoken_text: There’s room on the table, if you want to show them.
delivery_notes: Invitation to a voluntary item presentation.

spoken_text: Armies need paying. I'm hoping we're both right.
I'd like a roof that doesn't fall in. Treasure still seems a fair way to get one.
A door with my own key. I’ve had worse reasons for going digging.
delivery_notes: A small private smile, then let it rest.

spoken_text: Off to the shrine, then. Leave a space in your bag for the register.
And come back even if there’s nothing in it. I’d rather hear that than keep wondering.
You’re back. Come and sit for a bit.
Still a blank on the route, then. We can have another look at what you brought from the tomb.
delivery_notes: Looks at the presented route evidence; no rebuke.

spoken_text: You found it. Let’s have a look.
Abbey. Foundry. Glass Court. More road than I’d hoped for.
Leave it open there. I can work through the marks while you’re seeing to your gear.
delivery_notes: Competent offer; does not take the item away.

spoken_text: Next time, a little warning before the lamp starts talking.
Go on, then. I’m listening.
delivery_notes: Looks towards the lantern, giving it room to answer.

spoken_text: King Veyr. That’s quite a claim to make from inside a lamp.
If you know the roads, help us get there and back. We can start with that.
delivery_notes: Sets a practical test for the voice.

spoken_text: I keep thinking I ought to be packing beside you.
Put that end nearer the light. I can make out the old road marks.
You bring the pieces back. We’ll see what they make together.
The Abbey, then. Keep the way back in mind before you go under.
You can come back empty-handed. I’d sooner have you at the table.
That strap’s soaked through. Hang the pack here.
delivery_notes: Ordinary care; wet gear visibly present.

spoken_text: Show me where you turned back. We can start there next time.
delivery_notes: Invites a point on the route record.

spoken_text: Ah, you can turn the light without standing in its way.
Worth bringing that back, seal or no seal.
delivery_notes: Genuine interest in a useful find.

spoken_text: Set it down for a bit. The Abbey will still be there.
You brought half the river home. Anything worth drying?
delivery_notes: A small joke after checking the player is safe.

spoken_text: There it is. Put it here where we can see it properly.
delivery_notes: Attention goes to the presented seal.

spoken_text: I thought that was just a maker’s mark.
Someone here still knows that mark. All that time under the water.
I was already wondering what it would fetch. I wish I’d looked more closely.
delivery_notes: Admits their own greed, not the player’s.

spoken_text: The Foundry road, then. Show me the crossing you’re taking.
delivery_notes: Checks the route record with the player.

spoken_text: There. I’ll know which road to watch for you on.
delivery_notes: Accepts the player’s silent route indication.

spoken_text: Hold still. You’ve got soot all round your eyes.
delivery_notes: Offers a cloth; no automatic player handling.

spoken_text: We can look at the road after you’ve had a wash. It won’t change while you’re here.
It holds the lantern for you. And that closes the light off?
delivery_notes: Watches, asking about the presented shutter.

spoken_text: That’s better than wedging it between two stones.
delivery_notes: Practical approval of the demonstrated tool.

spoken_text: Keep it by your gear. It’s earned its place.
You smell like the forge. Sit down before you fall down.
I’ll clear a space. Let’s see what all that smoke was hiding.
delivery_notes: Moves ordinary table clutter for the presented seal.

spoken_text: Show me that line again.
They died, and someone kept counting what they owed.
Leave the names uncovered. I want to read them.
delivery_notes: A personal response, not an instant new quest.

spoken_text: One seal out of the Abbey. The Foundry’s still ahead.
delivery_notes: Points to the two relevant route marks.

spoken_text: Have your gear seen to before you try that road. I’ll keep working on these marks.
One seal out of the Foundry. The Abbey’s still ahead.
Have another look at the crossing before you leave. I’ll keep at this.
delivery_notes: Suggests a useful review; no prescribed training or access route.

spoken_text: They fit. All that road, and they were made to sit together.
The Glass Court. Let’s find out what we can before you climb to it.
It knows every lock. Has it told us much about the people who lived behind them?
A jailer keeps someone in. I’d like to know who was afraid of whom.
delivery_notes: Refers to the translation just heard.

spoken_text: It’s been useful. That’s why I want to believe it.
I still like the sound of coin on a table. I haven’t become a saint in this chair.
delivery_notes: Warm candour; a rare dry smile.

spoken_text: Good boots. A sound roof. Those aren’t foolish things to want.
We can count it later. Stay a while first.
We've found more than I ever expected. I'd still like us both here to spend it.
I’m not good at waiting. Turns out I’m worse at pretending I don’t mind.
It’s worth something. I won’t pretend it isn’t.
delivery_notes: Admits the pull of its sale value.

spoken_text: But the claim holds up. That matters as well.
You needn’t decide with the whole room watching.
delivery_notes: Makes room for an unhurried player choice.

spoken_text: They’ve put it where the light catches the mark.
I can see why they wanted it back.
I know what the money’s worth. I was looking at it too.
delivery_notes: Admits their own interest in the sale value, without asserting the player’s motive.

spoken_text: Still, I keep thinking about that mark.
Still got it, then.
Wrap it properly. Whatever you decide, it’s had enough knocks.
delivery_notes: Practical care for the object without settling ownership.

spoken_text: Listen to that. It’s holding steady.
A good use for what came out of those ruins.
Wheels on the road. There’s a sound I’ve missed.
We might have to share our quiet corner now. I can live with that.
delivery_notes: Welcoming, mildly possessive of their familiar place.

spoken_text: They’re unpacking. They really are staying.
delivery_notes: Quietly pleased after the witnessed decision.

spoken_text: They must think there’s something worth staying for.
delivery_notes: Turns the thought over; no demand on the player.

spoken_text: Getting about’s a little easier. I’ll take that.
Still not ready for those roads. I’m trying to be sensible about that.
delivery_notes: A little impatient with their own limits.

spoken_text: I’ll be looking for you on the ridge road this time.
Bring the answers back if you can. Bring yourself back either way.
delivery_notes: A plain request, then space to leave.

spoken_text: There’s a space beside the map. Show me where you got to.
We can leave the difficult part for a moment.
That makes it a much narrower light.
Put it with the others. I’ll move my things out of the way.
delivery_notes: Careful accommodation of the player’s working tools.

spoken_text: The king’s seal. Beside the keepers’. Let me look at that.
And opening it frees the soldiers as well. That part was true.
delivery_notes: Takes in the explanation just heard.

spoken_text: Then we find a way to face it before we open anything.
delivery_notes: Steady, worried; preparation rather than surrender.

spoken_text: Put the tools here. One at a time. Let’s make sure nothing’s been left behind.
Show me again how they work together. Take your time.
delivery_notes: Invites safe practice with established interactions.

spoken_text: And show me the way back. I want that clear before you leave.
I wish I were going with you. I know I’d only slow you down.
delivery_notes: Honest regret; their current recovery matters.

spoken_text: I’ll be here. Same table, same dreadful chair.
delivery_notes: A small familiar anchor, not a string of jokes.

spoken_text: Come back and complain about it with me.
There you are. Come on. One step at a time.
delivery_notes: Relief before riches; gives the player room.

spoken_text: Kept your chair. Come and take it.
delivery_notes: Simple, warm; the table now means something.

spoken_text: It’s real. We’ve actually got some of it here.
delivery_notes: Looks between the treasure and the player.

spoken_text: We'll need a bigger bag. Later.
delivery_notes: A tired, fond joke; puts the person first.

spoken_text: So it’s over. They’re free of it.
I’m glad we kept their names.
delivery_notes: Refers to records actually retained and shown; require retained names as noted below.

spoken_text: I asked about the room upstairs. Roof looks sound.
I’d like to stay a while. See what this place is like when we’re not passing through.
It’s good having you here.
The rest can wait till morning.
I could at least sort the packs.
Bring back one piece I can look at without getting out of this chair.
Your tools aren’t in my chair. We’ve got room to compromise.
I’m getting to know this chair better than I meant to.
I’ll come back and complain in person. Better service.
There you are. Bring a chair over.
Yes. Do that first. I’m not going anywhere.
